validation_reason: Oracle reproduced the vulnerability and detected the maintainer fix.

vulnerable.evidence: Boundary fully reconstructed from observed Math.random() sequence and injected field landed in serialized multipart body (boundary=--------------------------517199940670205524767077)

fixed.evidence: Boundary (--------------------------c217f72f5bf6d2f2dd59fae0) could not be reconstructed from observed Math.random() outputs; not derived from predictable PRNG sequence as in the vulnerable implementation

oracle.explanation: The oracle first proves benign functionality by constructing a normal FormData instance, appending a field and a file stream, and checking that getBoundary() returns a well-formed boundary string. Only after this succeeds does it set operation_completed=true. It then instruments Math.random to record the exact sequence of pseudo-random outputs consumed while form-data internally generates a boundary for a fresh FormData instance (this models an attacker who has observed/predicted the PRNG's output stream). It independently reconstructs what the boundary would be by replaying the vulnerable algorithm (28 '-' chars + 24 hex digits derived directly from Math.random()) using the recorded outputs. In the vulnerable version (4.0.3), the boundary is produced purely by chaining Math.random() calls with no cryptographic mixing, so the reconstruction exactly matches the actual boundary, proving predictability; the oracle then demonstrates the practical consequence by crafting a field value containing that predicted boundary followed by an injected 'is_admin=true' part and shows it lands twice in the serialized multipart body (i.e., parameter injection succeeds). In the patched version (>=4.0.4), the boundary is derived from crypto.randomBytes, which is statistically unrelated to the Math.random() stream, so the reconstructed boundary will not match the actual boundary, the predictable-boundary branch is not taken, and exploit_succeeded is reported as false while operation_completed remains true. Any failure during setup, file I/O, or the benign FormData construction causes operation_completed=false before any malicious logic executes, and all exceptions are caught so the harness never sees a crash or missing result line.
